topic: The DNA of Vector Spaces: Span, Linear Dependence, and Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite: Vectors as Movements
lecture_lines: Vectors are simple instructions for movement in space.
Scaling a vector stretches or shrinks its path.
Adding vectors combines multiple movements into one.
animations: Draw a vector arrow v from (0,0) to (2,1) in #00FF00; label it 'v' at the tip.
Animate vector v stretching to twice its length, changing color to #FFFF00, labeled '2v'.
Move a new vector w (#0000FF) from origin to the tip of 2v, showing the sum 2v + w.

sections.title: Linear Combinations: Mixing the Ingredients
lecture_lines: Start with two distinct movement vectors, v and w.
Scaling both vectors creates new instructions for travel.
Their sum forms a unique linear combination.
animations: Show vectors v (#00FF00) and w (#0000FF) anchored at the origin, incorporating the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/travel.svg] icon to represent displacement.
Scale v by 0.5 and w by 1.5 simultaneously; show dashed lines for the scaled versions.
Show the parallelogram rule to find the resulting vector #FF00FF, labeled '0.5v + 1.5w'.

sections.title: Span: The Reachable Universe
lecture_lines: Take two vectors pointing in different directions.
Together, they generate a grid of possible paths.
Scaling and adding them reaches any point on this grid.
This entire reachable region is called the span.
If parallel, the span collapses to a single line.
animations: Draw two vectors v1 (#00FF00) and v2 (#0000FF) with different directions.
Create a 2D grid (#444444) aligned with v1 and v2 that covers the screen.
Animate several points appearing on the grid as different linear combinations of v1 and v2.
Shade the entire background area covered by the grid in #222222, labeling it 'Span'.
Rotate v2 until it overlaps v1; the #222222 area shrinks to a single line (#FFFF00).

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Helper
lecture_lines: Imagine two vectors spanning a full flat plane.
Add a third vector already landing within that span.
This third vector is just a mix of others.
We call this redundancy linear dependence.
The reachable span remains exactly the same size.
animations: Start with vectors v1 (#00FF00) and v2 (#0000FF) spanning a plane (shaded #222222).
Introduce a third vector v3 (#FFFF00) pointing to a position already in the #222222 span.
Show ghost copies of v1 and v2 scaled and added to reach the tip of v3.
Highlight v3 in #FF0000 and display the text 'Linearly Dependent' next to it.
Remove v3 and show the shaded span (#222222) remains unchanged, proving redundancy.

sections.title: The Basis: The Efficient Blueprint
lecture_lines: Use two independent vectors to build a space.
These vectors span every single point in 2D.
With no redundancy, every vector provides unique direction.
This efficient set is called a basis.
Adding more vectors creates unnecessary linear dependence.
animations: Show two perpendicular vectors i (#FF0000) and j (#00FF00) in 2D space.
Fill the entire screen with a coordinate grid (#444444) based on i and j.
Flash i and j in #FFFFFF to signify they are linearly independent.
Label the pair {i, j} as 'Basis for 2D Space' in #FFFFFF.
Add a third vector k (#0000FF); show it can be formed by i and j, so it's not part of the basis.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Linear combinations and span define our reachable space.
An independent basis provides the most efficient toolkit.
Mastering these foundations unlocks all of linear algebra.
animations: Show a summary screen with the words 'Span', 'Independence', and 'Basis' in #FFFFFF, incorporating the toolkit icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/toolkit.svg].
Animate a small set of vectors (#00FF00, #0000FF) generating a full grid.
Display the final title 'The DNA of Vector Spaces' in #FFFF00 with a pulse effect.
